en.name: Katharine Drexel
en.summary: American banking heiress who gave away a vast personal fortune to found and fund schools and missions for Native American and African American communities.
en.body: Katharine Drexel was born into one of Philadelphia's wealthiest banking families and, after a private audience with Pope Leo XIII in which she asked him to send more missionaries to serve Native Americans, was reportedly told by the pope himself that she should become a missionary. She founded the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament for Indians and Colored People in 1891, and over the following decades personally funded and helped establish nearly 150 missions, schools, and Xavier University of Louisiana, the only historically Black Catholic university in the United States, using an inheritance worth many millions of dollars that she directed almost entirely to this work rather than personal use. She worked directly against the racial segregation and discrimination of her era, often facing intimidation for the interracial character of her schools. She died in 1955 and was canonized in 2000.
